research_rationale: EO 10054 (signed 1949-04-29, 14 FR 2129, read in full from the held official FR text, sha256 of the downloaded page file 02f3bed2...), one paragraph, modifies para. 3(a) of EO 9721 for one named person: the three-year limit is replaced by five years from the beginning of Gross's service with the International Telecommunication Union. EO 12553 (reading record LSP-EO_12553, read once in full; the table row '10054 Modifying provisions for transfer of personnel to certain public international organizations') revokes the order outright, with no effective-date wording; the claim therefore rests on the on_signing reading, 1986-02-25, and treats that date as an upper bound, not a certified end. Inventory: the dossier's single clause (chars 826-2170) covers the whole operative paragraph from 'By virtue of the authority' to the end of the proviso and the order has no other section; kept. Earlier-end tests. (1) Own terms: the order has no sunset or termination clause. The five-year period is a condition on when Gross's service must end to carry the reemployment right; it does not say the modification expires, and its start date (the unheld beginning of his service) is not needed to find an end because it is not an end. A window or report-type deadline is never an end. (2) Parent chain: Parent-order chain read in the held official texts: EO 9721 (11 FR 5209, May 10, 1946) para. 3(a) reemploys an employee whose international-organization service is 'terminated without prejudice within three years from the date of such transfer' and requires application within ninety days after termination; EO 9949 (13 FR 2089, 1948-04-17) gave the same five-year relief to Paul D. Miles; EO 10103 (1950-02-01) amends only secs. 1 and 2 of EO 9721 and does not touch para. 3(a) or name EO 10054; EO 10804 (24 FR 1147, signed 1959-02-12) sec. 2 revokes EO 9721, EO 10103 and EO 10774 'except that each shall be considered to remain in effect' for employees serving with an international organization on the enactment date of the Federal Employees International Organization Service Act (72 Stat. 961) who do not elect its coverage 'and for the purposes of any rights and benefits vested under each such order' before that date; EO 11138 (1964-01-07, Frederick Strauss) and EO 11303 (1966-09-12, Reginald C. Price) waive limits in EO 9721 for other named persons. EO 10804 names neither EO 10054, EO 9949 nor EO 10415, revokes only the parent, and expressly keeps rights vested under it; because Gross's window had closed by 1954-04-29 at the latest, nothing but already vested rights could remain under the modification in 1959, so the 1959 partial revocation of the parent neither ends nor changes this clause and is ruled out as an earlier end (it is not attachable as a structured later event because the dossier holds no ACT record for it; the held official text was read). EO 11138 and EO 11303 name other persons and EO 10103 does not touch para. 3(a), so all three are ruled out. EO 12553's table lists EO 9721, 9949, 10054, 10103, 10415, 11138 and 11303 at their own rows, so the whole family was swept by the same sentence on the same date. (3) The OFR note 'See: Transfer Order 40 of the Secretary of Defense dated July 22, 1949 (14 FR 4908)' is a cross-reference (edge LE-6bdb8b3573f1 is typed cross_reference); a departmental transfer order cannot amend or end an executive order and it does not name EO 10054; ruled out, not a later event. The dossier's machine 'termination' lead (EO 10054 against EO 9721, edge LE-f1e26f42aee9) is the order's own modifying sentence, not an end. (4) Statutory leads (Federal Employees International Organization Service Act, 72 Stat. 961, cited in EO 10804) are not held beyond that citation and are not express ends. The dossier has no missing lines and no conflicts. Later events attached: none, because none ends or changes this clause. Savings: transferred_or_accrued (see savings reason). Risk noted for the reviewer: a spent-by-exhaustion reading (window closed by 1954) would make EO 12553 only an upper bound; no source shows the exhaustion date, so the express revocation is used.

savings_residuals.reason: Reading record LSP-EO_12553 (ending instrument): one operative sentence ('to eliminate Executive Orders that are no longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked:') followed by a No./Subject table and the signature block 'THE WHITE HOUSE, February 25, 1986.'; it has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25 (the on_signing reading; Federal Register publication on 1986-03-03 is not an effective date); it has no savings, continuation, transfer, exception or delayed-effect provision. Own-residual check, reading EO 10054 in full: it creates no office, function, fund or property and sets no continuing duty. Its only substantive effect is a personal, conditional entitlement: Gerald C. Gross, if his Union service ends 'without prejudice within five years' of its beginning (before 1949-04-29, so by 1954-04-29 at the latest) and he meets the other conditions of EO 9721, 'shall be entitled to such reemployment rights'. Whether his service ended in that window and whether he was reemployed is unheld. Any right that vested when his service ended in the window is an effect of the order that EO 12553 (which saves nothing) does not undo and that EO 10804 sec. 2 itself preserved for rights 'vested under each such order'; the later employment status would rest on civil-service law, not on this order. S0 prefill (none_after_bounded_search) OVERRULED to transferred_or_accrued because of the conditional personal reemployment right; the accrual itself cannot be shown from held sources, which is why the state is recorded and not 'none'. Bounded search: every held official FR text under jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts (6,652 files) was grepped for the order's number, its subject words and the generic-reference phrases that could change it; the OFR catalog edges (jobs/later-events EDGES.csv, COUNTEREVIDENCE_LEADS.csv, UNPARSED_NOTE_SEGMENTS.csv), the dossier's current-law leads (none) and the three machine searches were read.
